header: Date: 2026-03-04 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 min | Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Tariq Osei (Redwood SE), Marta Lopez (Silverline Head of ML), Derek Chen (Silverline CTO), Aisha Khan (Silverline SRE), Samuel Ito (Silverline Data Scientist)
summary: POC scoping call to decide between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment modes for Silverline Retail's conversational and reranking workloads. Discussed success criteria (latency, throughput, cost, security), workload sizing, benchmark plan, timeline, networking/KMS requirements, and next steps for a 4-week POC. Security and compliance are the main drivers for Dedicated vs Private. Customer to provide traffic samples and prompts; Redwood to provide benchmark kit and pricing.
topics: Benchmarks and metrics (p95 latency, throughput TPS, cost per 1M tokens)
Deployment tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
Security requirements: SOC2, KMS, VPC peering
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're on the 4pm slot. quick roll call?
[00:06] Marta (Silverline): Marta here.
[00:08] Derek: Derek here.
[00:10] Aisha: Aisha here.
[00:12] Jordan: Great. Priya and Tariq are on from our SE team, Priya will lead the benchmarks discussion. 
[00:18] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all, quick agenda: confirm success criteria, get final sizing numbers, align on what we run in the POC (models, prompt sets), and outline network/security needs.
[00:28] Samuel (Silverline): Sounds good. For context, we want to replace parts of our product search assistant and a reranker for internal merch decisions. Main KPIs are p95 latency under 200ms for interactive prompts and throughput to support ~40 concurrent user flows at peak which roughly maps to 40 tps for simple text generation, and around 10 RPS for reranking batch jobs.
[00:45] Priya: Helpful. When you say 200ms p95, is that end-to-end including network or just inference time?
[00:51] Marta: Ideally end-to-end but we can be pragmatic. If we can keep inference at ~100ms p95 then we can meet app level 200ms with our infra.
[00:58] Jordan: Great, so success criteria is: inference p95 < 120ms, throughput 50 TPS sustained, 99.9% availability during the test, and unit cost target - do you have a target cost per 1M tokens?
[01:12] Derek: We're aiming to keep cost similar to our current managed provider, around $X per million tokens - I didn't bring exact number but will share. Cost sensitivity is medium-high. Security is high.
[01:22] Priya: Ok noted. Quick question on datasets: for reranking, are you running batches or streaming?
[01:28] Samuel: Batch nightly for large sets, but we also have ad-hoc reranks during campaigns. So both.
[01:33] Priya: Makes sense, Redwood supports mixed workloads - the difference between Hosted/Dedicated/Private comes down to isolation, predictable latency under load, and networking restrictions.
[01:44] Jordan: I'll summarize tradeoffs high-level: Hosted = fastest to get started, lower ops overhead, pay-as-you-go, but less control over VPC and bring-your-own-KMS. Dedicated = reserved GPU pools for you, predictable throughput and better isolation, can meet stricter latency SLOs, still managed by Redwood. Private = customer-managed control plane or on-prem, full network control, best for strict compliance, higher setup and ops work and lead time.
[02:07] Aisha: For us, the sticking point is KMS and no egress to unknown 3rd parties. We need SSO/SAML for users, SOC2 reports, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[02:18] Tariq: We do SOC2 and ISO support for Dedicated and Private; audit logs and SSO can be integrated. For Private we can do customer-managed KMS or HSM, for Dedicated we offer KMS integration into customer KMS in many cases.
[02:29] Marta: If Dedicated can give us KMS and VPC peering for the control plane, that might be acceptable and cheaper than Private. But what about latency variations at peak - you mentioned predictable throughput, how do you guarantee that?
[02:41] Priya: Dedicated is a reserved pool; you get pinned capacity so noisy neighbor risk is low. We also surface per-route latency dashboards and can set concurrency limits. We'll recommend specific GPU types and quantization to hit your p95 targets.
[02:53] Samuel: Which models are you recommending? We're currently using an open LLM for general generation and a specialized smaller reranker.
[02:59] Priya: For gen, we typically recommend a 7B or 13B variant with quantization for latency-sensitive endpoints. For rerank, a distilled encoder or dedicated cross-encoder model. For the POC we can run both a smaller fast model and a higher-quality model for comparison.
[03:14] Jordan: Timeline - we're proposing a 4-week POC: week 0-1 onboarding & infra config, week 2 benchmarks + smoke tests, week 3 resilience tests and quality evals, week 4 review and handoff. Does that align?
[03:25] Derek: That timeline could work, but we'll need to slot time for legal review if Dedicated or Private are selected. Procurement adds 2-3 weeks typically.
[03:32] Priya: Understood. For the POC we can run Hosted initially to get quick results while we parallel-path Dedicated/Private legal and networking. That reduces blocker risk.
[03:41] Marta: Would results on Hosted be comparable to Dedicated? I worry about noisy neighbor effects making our data noisy.
[03:46] Priya: Benchmarks on Hosted are a good proxy for per-request correctness and relative quality, but raw latency and tail behavior are best measured on Dedicated because of reserved capacity. Our POC plan includes both: run functional and quality tests on Hosted for quick wins; then repeat the key latency/throughput benchmarks on Dedicated hardware we provision for you.
[04:02] Aisha: For Private, what's the typical lead time and what responsibilities fall to us?
[04:07] Tariq: For on-prem or VPC Private, lead time is usually 6-10 weeks depending on networking approvals and KMS procurement. Customer needs to provide networking, firewall rules, access to their KMS, and some ops to help with installation. We also provide an installer and runbooks.
[04:20] Derek: That's a long tail. Cost-wise, how should we think about Dedicated vs Private?
[04:25] Jordan: Dedicated is billed as reserved capacity monthly, so predictable OPEX. Private often has an initial platform fee plus support and potentially higher infra cost if self-hosted. We'll include estimates in the pricing doc.
[04:34] Priya: For benchmarks, here's what we'll run: 1) Latency microbench (single-request p50/p95), 2) Sustained throughput ramp to your target TPS, 3) Cold-start and KV-cache warm scenarios if you use chat-like flows, 4) Quality evals with your prompt set and reference answers, 5) Cost-projection analysis using measured tokens/sec for each config. We'll give scripts to simulate your traffic and collect p95, p99, CPU/GPU utilization and cost estimates.
[04:56] Samuel: On traffic simulation - we'll provide a two-week sample of real traffic; is that sufficient?
[05:00] Priya: Two weeks of representative traffic plus the top 50-100 prompts is ideal. That lets us measure distribution and tail events. Please sanitize any PII before sending.
[05:08] Aisha: On networking, we need VPC peering or private link options; we can't have public internet egress from the inference VMs.
[05:15] Tariq: We support VPC peering and private link for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we have private link options in select regions; otherwise Hosted will use TLS over public endpoints. We'll include the exact network diagram in the follow-up.
[05:28] Jordan: Great, I'll capture the decision criteria we discussed: 1) If security is the top blocker (KMS/HSM, no egress, strict audits) -> Private. 2) If you want predictable latency with less ops burden -> Dedicated. 3) If you want fastest time-to-value and flexible pay-as-you-go -> Hosted. Also consider cost sensitivity and procurement timelines.
[05:47] Marta: That matches our internal thinking. We lean Dedicated if the pricing is within 15% of our current spend and KMS integration is supported. Private only if Dedicated can't meet KMS or data residency needs.
[05:58] Priya: For the POC we propose: start Hosted for quality and functional tests immediately, provision a short-lived Dedicated pool in week 2 for latency and throughput benchmarks, and run a Private feasibility assessment in parallel if you want. We'll provide cost delta estimates.
[06:11] Derek: One more ask - can you provide SOC2 report and a sample security checklist for our InfoSec?
[06:16] Jordan: Yes, we'll attach SOC2, ISO docs, and a checklist in the follow-up.
[06:21] Samuel: About model drift monitoring - do you provide quality regression alerts?
[06:25] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize has built-in quality monitoring tied to eval prompt sets; we can include that as part of the POC baseline.
[06:31] Aisha: Ok, recap next steps?
[06:34] Jordan: Recap: Jordan sends pricing + Private one-pager by Friday 3/6; Priya shares benchmark kit and scripts by Thursday 3/5; Marta and team to provide prompt set and two weeks of traffic by Monday 3/9; schedule technical deep-dive on networking/KMS for 3/10. We'll run Hosted tests first and spin up Dedicated for latency runs in week 2.
[06:51] Derek: Thanks all.
[06:53] Marta: Thanks, talk soon.
[06:55] Jordan: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
[06:59] End of recording.
